summary.title: Green-Schwarz, Nambu-Goto Actions, and Cayley's Hyperdeterminant
summary.executive_summary: This paper demonstrates that the Nambu-Goto (NG) action for the Green-Schwarz (GS) sigma-model of N=2 superstring in D=2+2 dimensions can be reformulated using Cayley's hyperdeterminant. By eliminating the zweibein field via its non-algebraic field equation, the authors derive an action where the kinetic term is the square root of Cayley's hyperdeterminant of the superspace pull-back, manifestly invariant under SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR). This reformulation preserves fermionic kappa-symmetry, ensuring classical equivalence to the Neveu-Schwarz-Ramond (NSR) formulation. The work highlights the suitability of D=2+2 target superspace for self-dual supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory and integrable models, linking these concepts through the hyperdeterminant structure.

Executive Summary
This paper demonstrates that the Nambu-Goto (NG) action for the Green-Schwarz (GS) sigma-model of N=2 superstring in D=2+2 dimensions can be reformulated using Cayley's hyperdeterminant. By eliminating the zweibein field via its non-algebraic field equation, the authors derive an action where the kinetic term is the square root of Cayley's hyperdeterminant of the superspace pull-back, manifestly invariant under SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR). This reformulation preserves fermionic kappa-symmetry, ensuring classical equivalence to the Neveu-Schwarz-Ramond (NSR) formulation. The work highlights the suitability of D=2+2 target superspace for self-dual supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory and integrable models, linking these concepts through the hyperdeterminant structure.

Research Context
Cayley's hyperdeterminant has found applications in quantum information and black hole entropy. Nambu-Goto action in D=2+2 possesses manifest SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) symmetry. D=2+2 is the consistent target space-time for N=2 NSR superstring. NSR formulation has drawbacks due to fermionic superpartners on the 2D world-sheet. Green-Schwarz formulation lacks explicit world-sheet supersymmetry but is classically equivalent. The kinetic term in the GS action is not of the NG-type equivalent to a Cayley's hyperdeterminant. Self-dual supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory can accommodate the D=2+2 target space-time.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study asks if the N=2 GS sigma-model shares the hyperdeterminant feature of the NG action. The hypothesis is that eliminating the zweibein reveals the NG action as the square root of Cayley's hyperdeterminant. The authors predict the resulting action will be invariant under SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR). It is hypothesized that the action retains fermionic kappa-symmetry despite metric elimination. The target superspace D=(2,2;2,2) is expected to support self-dual supersymmetric Yang-Mills. The study aims to confirm classical equivalence to the NSR formulation via kappa-symmetry.

Methodological Details
The study focuses on N=2 superstring with target space-time D=2+2. The formulation uses the Green-Schwarz sigma-model with N=(1,1) supersymmetry. The target superspace is defined as D=(2,2;2,2) with 2+2 bosonic and fermionic coordinates. The fundamental field variable is the superspace coordinate ZM. The action involves the superspace pull-back defined as PiA = (partial i ZM) EM A. The metric etaab has signature diag(+, +, -, -) for the D=2+2 space-time. The flat background vielbein EM A is explicitly constructed using sigma matrices. The fermionic indices alpha and .alpha correspond to chiral and anti-chiral coordinates. The study eliminates the zweibein field via its non-algebraic field equation. The elimination procedure is analogous to obtaining NG action from Polyakov action.

Procedures And Architectures
The total action I is defined as the integral of the Lagrangian L over d2sigma. The Lagrangian consists of an NG-term and a WZNW-term. The NG-term is the square root of the determinant of Gammaij. Gammaij is defined as the product of pull-backs Pi a Pi j a. The WZNW-term involves the antisymmetric tensor superfield BAB. Local light-cone coordinates + and - are defined by projectors P and Q. The square root of Gammaij, denoted gamma, is defined by gamma i(k) gamma j(k) = Gammaij. The Virasoro conditions Gamma++ = 0 and Gamma-- = 0 are derived as constraints. Cayley's hyperdeterminant Det(Pi i alpha .alpha) is related to det(Gammaij) by a factor of -1. The global symmetry is proven via infinitesimal transformations of SL(2, IR) groups. Fermionic kappa-symmetry is verified by showing delta_kappa I = 0. The derivation starts from the conventional GS sigma-model action IGS. The 2D metric field equation gij. is solved to eliminate the metric. The on-shell relationship between zweibein ei(j) and gamma i(j) is established.

Key Results
The NG action is re-expressed as the square root of Cayley's hyperdeterminant. The action exhibits manifest SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) symmetry. The square root of Det(Pi i alpha .alpha) equals the square root of -det(Gammaij). The Virasoro conditions Gamma++ = 0 and Gamma-- = 0 are satisfied. The action possesses fermionic kappa-symmetry. The action is classically equivalent to the N=2 NSR superstring. The target superspace accommodates self-dual supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. The hidden discrete symmetry of triality is absent in the N=2 string case. The elimination of the zweibein results in an action independent of the 2D metric. The superspace pull-back Pi i alpha .alpha plays the key role for the manifest symmetry.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The reformulation elucidates the global SL(2, IR) symmetry via Cayley's hyperdeterminant. The D=2+2 signature is crucial because SO(2,2) approx SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR). Non-manifest symmetries become manifest after eliminating auxiliary fields. The action suggests ZM alone are suitable for discussing global symmetry. SDSYM theory is the underlying theory for supersymmetric integrable systems in D<=3. The work links Cayley's hyperdeterminant to N=2 superstring and integrable models.

Contradictions And Limitations
The quantum-level equivalence of NG action to Polyakov action is not well established. The authors do not claim quantum equivalence to conventional N=2 NSR or GS string. The hidden discrete symmetry of triality is absent due to the WZNW-term. The number of world-sheet supersymmetries should not be confused with space-time supersymmetries. The paper focuses only on N=(1,1) supersymmetry in D=2+2.

Claims
The N=2 GS sigma-model action can be reformulated using Cayley's hyperdeterminant after eliminating the zweibein. Nambu-Goto action can be re-expressed in terms of Cayley's hyperdeterminant it contains the Nambu-Goto action which is nothing but the square root of Cayley's hyperdeterminant hidden discrete symmetry ... seems absent in N = 2 string elucidate the global SL(2, IR) symmetry of the latter
The reformulated action possesses fermionic kappa-symmetry and is classically equivalent to the NSR formulation. satisfying the criterion for its light-cone equivalence to Neveu-Schwarz-Ramond formulation fermionic kappa-invariance delta_kappa I = 0  classically equivalent to NSR N = 2 superstring

Data And Code Availability
The paper is a theoretical derivation without experimental data or code.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The derivation is justified by comparing with the conventional GS sigma-model.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the reformulation of N=2 GS action using Cayley's hyperdeterminant. 2. The strongest evidence is the demonstration of manifest SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) x SL(2, IR) symmetry. 3. The future path involves exploring supersymmetric integrable models in D<=3.
